Tulalip

The Tulalip Tribes brings together histories of Snohomish, Snoqualmie, Skykomish and allied peoples. These readings pair a community-authored account of organizing with Hibulb Cultural Center’s approach to public cultural education.

01

Identity and context

The Tulalip Tribes is a contemporary confederated government in the Puget Sound region.

Read the sources [1] The Tulalip Tribes

02

A path for deeper reading

Focus the next stage of research on: Constituent peoples, Lushootseed, treaty histories and community-published accounts. The sources below are selected reading paths; their authorship, dates and community scope should guide how they are used.

Read the sources [1] The Tulalip Tribes [2] tulaliptribes-nsn.gov

03

Community histories of organizing

An account credited to Wayne Williams, George Williams, Bernice Williams and Arnold McKay describes elders choosing representatives for intertribal meetings and later efforts to build a tribal government. It follows collective fundraising, council organization and land reacquisition. These are the named authors’ historical account; the original legal and administrative records remain further reading.

Read the sources [1] The Tulalip Tribes

04

Tulalip-led interpretation at Hibulb

Hibulb’s teacher guide introduces the histories of the peoples connected with Tulalip through English and Lushootseed interpretation. Its gallery guide brings waterways, canoes, schooling and community history into an educational path. Reading this guide does not mean the directory has examined its objects, heard its recordings or obtained permission to reproduce its displays.

Read the sources [3] Hibulb Cultural Center and Natural History Preserve

Tulalip History ↗

Two substantial narratives describe boarding-school experiences and twentieth-century organizing. The second is credited to Wayne Williams, George Williams, Bernice Williams and Arnold McKay; their historical interpretation remains attributed.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Complete Life in the Tulalip Indian Boarding School and Tulalip History Since World War I narrative units, including text after More controls. The separate chronology is not used as an independently checked timeline.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Public source body inspected through the web reader and/or a normal HTTP200 local copy. Linked recordings, original records, objects and photographs were not automatically inspected or licensed. No login, paywall bypass or outreach. Original school records, constitutional documents, litigation and land transactions were not independently inspected. No current finances, officeholders, legal holdings or universal constituent-community views are inferred.
